Phase "Quick fixes" — your July 1 items, live

Five items from your list, shipped and verified on production yesterday afternoon. Each one shown as it renders today.

The "duplicate" QSP question — resolved without deleting anything. LIVE As flagged in yesterday's investigation, the survey deliberately carries three "share the stories" slots (that's how the original Esperto questionnaire works, and each slot's historical answers are mapped separately). Deleting one would have broken the import mapping — so the three slots now label themselves (Story 1 of 3), (Story 2 of 3), (Story 3 of 3). Respondents see immediately that it's intentional.
Suzanne's wording fixes, in the live questionnaire. LIVE "Leadership Team" is now sentence-cased to match its 13 sibling factors, and the core-values question uses your suggested rewording — it no longer assumes a company has no values yet: "What are your core values? If not yet set, what do you think the top 3 should be?"
The invitation email your clients now receive — rendered by the exact same live email engine that sent the launch-test invitation (and matching the copy received in the test inbox July 2, byte for byte). LIVE Three of your four email asks in one frame: the coach's logo sits in the branded header, the body now says who invited them by name ("You've been invited by Gabriel Test…" — your coaches' names appear automatically), and the button is the large, unmissable version. The fourth ask — your revised body copy — drops straight in whenever you send it; the plumbing is already live.
Before"a responder has completed the assessment" — the email to the coach when someone finished, whenever the roster had no name on file.
After — live"maria@clientco.com has completed the assessment" — when there's no name, every coach-facing surface (emails and on-screen reports) now shows the respondent's email instead. Respondents themselves never see this fallback — their own greeting stays warm.

The "a responder" fix, shown as copy rather than a screenshot — it only appears when a roster entry has a blank name, which no live campaign has today. The logic is live and test-covered on production.

Your #18 ("possible duplicate") — checked against the source: not a duplicate. The original Esperto questionnaire asks the "most important thing" question three times on purpose, cascading from organization → year → quarter. All three exist in the source, so all three stay — same ruling as the story slots: faithful to the instrument, now visibly deliberate.

Phase "Admin & coach controls" — live last night

Your #1, #6 and #7, built and launched behind the usual safety switch. Below is the walkthrough, the way you or Suzanne would use each control.

Retire a template so nobody starts new campaigns on it (your #6)

Where you go: Assessments → Templates. Every template row now carries a Disable action — and this screenshot shows the real current state: Quarterly Session Prep v1 is already disabled (we retired it at launch, since v2 replaced it). Note its badge and the action flipped to Enable — one click undoes it, any time.
platformtest.scalingup.com says

Disable template "Quarterly Session Prep v1"? Hidden from new-campaign setup. Existing campaigns and reports are not affected.

CancelOK

The confirmation you see when clicking Disable — reproduced here verbatim (browser confirm dialogs can't be screenshotted).

And here's the effect, from a coach's seat — captured this morning logged in as a coach: the new-campaign template picker offers QSP v2, but v1 is simply gone. The platform also refuses v1 at the server if anything tries to sneak past the picker. Running v1 campaigns, their reports, and their history are untouched — retiring a template never breaks the past.

Set "send results to respondents" as a template default (your #1)

Where you go: any template's editor → Metadata → the Results Email card. The new switch — "Send results to respondents by default" — makes the wizard's results-email checkbox start pre-ticked for every new campaign on that template. Coaches keep the override: they can still untick it per campaign, which is exactly the shape you asked for. The hint below the switch is the one honest catch: the default kicks in once that template's results-email content is approved (the existing safety gate that stops unreviewed email copy going to clients).

Remove an admin who's left the company (your #7)

Where you go: Admin Settings → Admin Users. The card now lists the actual admin accounts (not just invites) with their roles, and every row has Remove — except your own, so nobody can lock themselves out. Removal keeps all their history (everything they ever created stays attributed), and the email can be re-invited later if someone returns.
platformtest.scalingup.com says

Remove gabriel+waveq-drill@chiefaiofficer.com? They are locked out immediately. Their history is kept and the email can be re-invited.

CancelOK

The Remove confirmation, verbatim — from last night's live drill on a throwaway account created just to be removed.

» probe: open the admin dashboard with each account's still-valid login session
active admin session → 200 — dashboard renders
removed admin session (same kind of session, minutes after removal) → 307 — thrown out to the login screen
The part you can't screenshot — proven on production. "Removed" would be hollow if a departed admin's already-logged-in browser kept working (sessions normally live 30 days). So we removed a real throwaway admin during the launch and probed both ways: a live admin's session renders the dashboard; the removed admin's identical session is rejected on its very next request. Lock-out is immediate — and deliberately not reversible by the emergency kill-switch: turning the feature off stops further removals, it never lets a removed person back in.
